title: Stage skill generation and overrides
responsibility: Generate one packaged skill per canonical stage definition, named `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, so that stage purpose, decision owner, outputs and exit criteria are never hand-maintained twice; fail a check that writes nothing when a packaged stage skill is stale, missing or orphaned relative to `stages/`; and let a consumer override a packaged stage skill without editing the tool clone, through the project-settings `skills` entry for the consumer's override directory: Pi resolves project-settings skill paths ahead of package resources and the first skill with a given identity wins, so the consumer's override wins over the packaged skill of that identity.
notes: ⚠️ THE GENERATOR EXISTS TO PREVENT ONE SPECIFIC DRIFT: the agent working confidently to exit criteria the application is not checking. Two hand-maintained descriptions of one pipeline disagree, and the disagreement is invisible from either side. ⚠️ THE NAMING RULE IS A CONTRACT (2026-09-13). Every generated skill is `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, at `pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-<stage-id>/SKILL.md`, with that name in its frontmatter - for example `kiln-stage-01-intake` and `kiln-stage-09-handoff`. The prefix keeps them from colliding with a consumer's own skills, and the full name is the identity a consumer override must match, so it does not change without a migration. ⚠️ GENERATED AND HANDWRITTEN ARE KEPT APART. The generator owns exactly the `kiln-stage-*` skills and nothing else under `pi-package/skills/`. `kiln-planning` is handwritten, and generation and the check must never adopt it, rewrite it, report it as orphaned, or delete it; a skill directory the generator did not produce is not the generator's to judge. ⚠️ PURPOSE IS PART OF THIS COMPONENT, AND IT IS DEFERRED (F88, 2026-09-13). The responsibility above includes a stage's purpose, and the completed component will generate it. TSK-0046 does not, because no canonical purpose field exists today: `producesProse` describes what a stage produces, and printing it as a purpose would be inference rather than generation. TSK-0071 authors a purpose field in every definition and generates it from there; until then each generated skill states plainly that its purpose is not declared. ⚠️ OVERRIDE PRECEDENCE IS PI'S RESOLUTION ORDER, NOT REGISTRATION ORDER (F91, 2026-09-13). The override does not win by being registered after the packaged set; Pi 0.84.4 ranks a project-settings skill path ahead of a package resource and keeps the first skill with each name. The promise is that the consumer override wins over the packaged skill, not over every project skill path: an earlier project-settings entry holding the same identity outranks Kiln's appended override entry (R8).
